name: Burkina Faso

findings.summary: Smart Burkina: Huawei and CITCC installed a city video-surveillance and security-radio system with over 900 cameras at 300+ sites in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso, financed by a China Eximbank concessional loan; phase 1 ended April 2025.

sources.publisher: Government of Burkina Faso information service

findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: Huawei is the equipment vendor. Launch date 2021-07-08; loan signed 2020-09-29 per AidData. Tier 5 because the January 2026 government note reports a 900+ camera network and phase 1 finished (88.71% physical execution at 30 April 2025); APA reports real-time surveillance operational from April 2025 but names no vendor, so linking it to Smart Burkina is inference. US$94m is Ecofin's conversion of CFA 52bn; AidData gives the contract as about US$80m. Phase 2 (AI predictive analytics, automated fines) is still under financing negotiation. AidData coded S2 as a specialist research dataset.

findings.summary: The same Smart Burkina package funds about 650 km of Huawei-built national fibre backbone plus 150 km of metropolitan fibre linking cities, alongside a professional radio network for security forces.

sources.publisher: Government of Burkina Faso information service

findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Huawei, so prc. Tier 4 (construction under way, phase 1 near complete per the government note); not coded 5 because operational status of the fibre itself is not stated. Value carried on BFA-001 to avoid double-counting the single package. Ecofin gives 800 km in total, consistent with 650+150.

findings.summary: Huawei began building phase one of Burkina Faso's 2,001 km national fibre backbone in December 2017, under French supervisor Tactis, funded by a 12-year Bank of China/BNP Paribas loan; phase one cost about CFA 50bn.
findings.analyst_inference: US$180m is ITWeb's estimate for the full backbone (CFA 100bn); phase one about US$90m. Pre-2020; completion and current operation not confirmed. A 2014 CIO Mag piece described a larger 5,000 km Huawei backbone at CFA 120bn, so scope changed over time. Both sources may derive from one release.

findings.summary: A 2018 Safe City pilot with Huawei Technologies began with 45 camera sites, two years before the Smart Burkina project was formally created.

sources.publisher: Government of Burkina Faso information service

findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 (pilot). City not named in the note; scale subnational assumed (Ouagadougou likely). Superseded by BFA-001.

findings.financier: Danida Business Finance with Nordea Bank (partial)
findings.summary: Works began in September 2015 on the G-Cloud government cloud: eight nodes in six localities with servers, storage and e-trust services, linked by 741 km of fibre, delivered by Alcatel-Lucent and partly Danish-financed; CFA 36bn, 27-month schedule.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor Alcatel-Lucent (French, absorbed by Finnish Nokia in 2016), so third. Cost given as CFA 47bn in 2014 and CFA 36bn in 2015; not converted. Layer networks because fibre and network nodes dominate, though it is also a government cloud. Pre-2020; completion and current status not confirmed; the 2026 modular data centres are labelled 'Cloud gouvernemental' and may be its successor.

findings.controller: Ministry of Digital Transition, Burkina Faso
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Transition, Burkina Faso
findings.summary: The prime minister inaugurated two modular government-cloud data centres in Ouagadougou (3,000 TB storage, 28,800 CPU cores, 7,000+ VMs, about CFA 15bn) under a 'zero data abroad' repatriation policy; a larger national data centre is planned for 2028.
findings.analyst_inference: State-owned and operated, so domestic. Equipment vendor, builder and financier not named in any source, so those stay null; under the equipment rule the IT-equipment vendor could warrant a separate finding. US$28.6m is Afrique IT News's own conversion. Afrique IT News coded S2 as specialist tech press; if a reviewer treats it as S3 this falls to uncorroborated/low.

silicon.null_reason: no dedicated search; no accelerator purchases surfaced in network, data-centre or AI searches

models.null_reason: one AI/Russia search found an AI roadmap, parliamentary AI training and an April 2026 Russian public-diplomacy audience on AI/cyber skills training, but no model-provider adoption or national model

power.null_reason: Rosatom nuclear-plant agreements (2023 MOU, 2025 accord) surfaced but are not AI- or data-centre-specific

research_gaps: Radio/core vendors of Orange Burkina, Moov Africa Burkina (Maroc Telecom) and Telecel Faso were not established; one search and the Orange 4G launch article named none.
Who supplied the IT equipment and built the two January 2026 modular government data centres, and who is contracted for the planned 2028 national data centre?
Was the 2017 Huawei/Bank of China national backbone and the 2015 Alcatel-Lucent G-Cloud completed, and are they still in service?
Smart Burkina phase 2 (AI predictive analytics, automated traffic fines): financier and vendor under negotiation; check for a new China Eximbank loan.

Russian digital cooperation (Russian Centre for Public Diplomacy, Novosibirsk university schooling programme) is training-only so far; watch for any equipment or platform deal. A UAE digital-expertise lead (osiris.sn headline) was not opened.
